note: Unselected T2D; the members are engineered basal insulins (degludec approved 2015, icodec and efsitora 2026; peglispro stopped 2015 on liver fat/ALT, oral insulin 338 stopped after phase 2 on dose size; ex1000 could not be identified), all built on the same pig-clamp / rat-dog PK pharmacology.
label: Type 2 diabetes (insulin analogs)

engagement.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
engagement.note: Novo's 2006 pig clamp profiled degludec (insulin 454) against glargine; no human clamp comparison yet.
engagement.short: Pig clamp profiles degludec vs glargine
engagement.quote: Action profile of insulin 454 (0.6 mM and 1.2 mM) or Glargine (0.6 mM). A euglycaemic clamp study in pigs [by Novo Nordisk A/S, Denmark]
engagement.confidence_note: Study 6UIR050902 is dated March 2006 in the review; the review itself was public in 2015, so 2006 is a proxy opening date.

engagement.model: Conscious dog euglycaemic clamp with hepatic balance
engagement.note: Peglispro (LY2605541) switched dog liver to net glucose uptake while sparing non-hepatic uptake; no human clamp yet.
engagement.quote: In contrast to exogenously administered human insulin, LY demonstrated preferential hepatic effects, similar to endogenously secreted insulin.

engagement.model: Conscious dog euglycaemic clamp with hepatic balance
engagement.note: Tracer clamps in healthy men and T1D patients reproduced the dog's hepato-preferential pattern (EGP suppressed at lower exposure than peripheral disposal). Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
engagement.quote: BIL has been demonstrated in a dog model, in healthy men and in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D) to have significant hepato-preferential action resulting from reduced peripheral activity.
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor-authored overview, abstract-level; the human clamps are in healthy volunteers and T1D, not T2D patients. The T1D clamp is Mudaliar 2016 (doi:10.1111/dom.12753).
engagement.reason: Dog hepato-preference held in human clamps
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the source itself puts the dog model and the human clamps side by side and the readout (hepatic vs peripheral glucose flux under euglycaemic clamp) moved the same way. Humans were healthy men and T1D patients; engagement admits healthy volunteers, and no T2D clamp with hepatic balance was found. Direction only; the dog exposures are not matched to human ones in the abstract.
engagement.magnitude_basis: hepatic vs non-hepatic glucose uptake under euglycaemic clamp

engagement.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
engagement.note: Icodec's human clamp in T2D showed glucose-lowering spread evenly over the 7-day interval, the sustained action the pig and dog clamps had shown. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
engagement.short: Weekly glucose-lowering held in T2D clamp
engagement.quote: insulin icodec was well tolerated and has pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic properties that are suited for once-weekly dosing, with a mean half-life of 196 hours and close to even distribution of glucose-lowering effect over the entire dosing interval of 1 week.
engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor-authored; the animal clamp and rat/dog PK data are in the FDA pharmacology review, not in this paper, so the pairing is the drafter's. Abstract-level.
engagement.reason: Clamp glucose-lowering held across the week
engagement.judgement: Called same: the model's readout (glucose infusion rate under euglycaemic clamp, sustained over the dosing interval) moved in dosed T2D patients for icodec; the same clamp readout held earlier for degludec (BEGIN clamps) and for efsitora (FDA integrated review, 2026). Comparison not stated in one source; FDA's 2026 icodec review supplies the animal side (sustained glucose lowering in diabetic rats and normoglycaemic dogs and pigs). Direction only.
engagement.magnitude_basis: glucose infusion rate profile over the dosing interval

engagement.note: Lilly's STZ-diabetic rat gave peglispro a prolonged duration of glucose lowering vs lispro; opening entry, no human comparison drawn yet.
engagement.short: STZ rat: peglispro prolonged glucose lowering
engagement.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. 2016 is the publication date (epub 2016-03-29); the rat studies were run before the IMAGINE phase 3 programme (2011) but no earlier citable source was found, so 2016 is a proxy for first use.

engagement.note: Healthy-subject euglycaemic clamps: peglispro glucose infusion rate sustained ≥36 h while glargine waned at 24 h, the prolonged action the STZ rat showed. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
engagement.short: Human clamp: peglispro GIR sustained ≥36 h
engagement.quote: LY2605541 glucose infusion rate (GIR) profiles were sustained for ≥36 hours versus glargine GIR profiles, which waned at 24 hours.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. The human clamp (epub 2014-02-13) predates the rat paper (2016-03-29); the entry is dated 2016, when the pairing first became possible. Healthy volunteers, not T2D patients.
engagement.judgement: Same, direction only: the rat's readout (duration of glucose lowering after one SC dose, longer than the short-acting comparator) moved the same way in dosed humans (GIR sustained >=36 h vs glargine 24 h). Pairing is the drafter's; the rat exposures are not matched to human ones in either abstract. This is the same Lilly STZ-rat system later used for efsitora (Moyers 2022), so peglispro opens the track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: duration of glucose-lowering action after a single subcutaneous dose vs comparator insulin

engagement.note: Efsitora in T2D patients and healthy subjects: t1/2 ~17 days and a sustained dose-dependent fall in fasting glucose for >=5 days after one dose, as the STZ rat (>=1 week) had shown. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
engagement.short: Efsitora: week-long glucose lowering held in T2D
engagement.quote: BIF had a PK half-life of approximately 17 days, which led to a sustained, dose-dependent decrease in fasting blood glucose for 5 days or longer.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; sponsor-authored phase 1 (single ascending dose in healthy participants and T2D; multiple dose in T2D). Pairing with the STZ rat is the drafter's.
engagement.reason: Rat's week-long glucose lowering held in humans
engagement.judgement: Second member on the track, entered as strengthens: the STZ rat predicted glucose lowering to normoglycaemia for at least a week after one SC dose of efsitora (Moyers 2022; FDA 761408 integrated review lines 1125-1127), and single doses in humans lowered fasting glucose for 5 days or longer with a flat weekly profile (peak-to-trough 1.14 at steady state). Direction only on the PD readout; the rat under-predicted the PK half-life (~120 h vs ~17 days), which is scored on the dose cell.
engagement.magnitude_basis: duration of fasting-glucose lowering after a single subcutaneous dose

dose.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
dose.note: Pig clamp and rat/dog PK set the protraction target for degludec; human half-life not yet measured.
dose.quote: Action profile of insulin 454 (0.6 mM and 1.2 mM) or Glargine (0.6 mM). A euglycaemic clamp study in pigs [by Novo Nordisk A/S, Denmark]
dose.confidence_note: Proxy opening date (study dated March 2006; review public 2015).

dose.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
dose.note: FDA set icodec's animal half-lives (25-61 h in rat, dog, pig) beside the human 173 h: the once-weekly regimen was reached and under-predicted ~3x. Dated 2021 (rule 6): Kjeldsen 2021 first set the dog screen beside icodec's 196 h human half-life. Retrodiction ruling: icodec's own once-weekly phase 2 (Rosenstock 2020, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2022474) was public before the dog/rat data, so retro.
dose.short: Weekly regimen reached; animals under-predicted t1/2 ~3x
dose.quote: Insulin icodec was selected by screening for long intravenous plasma half-life in dogs while ensuring glucose-lowering potency following subcutaneous administration in rats.
dose.confidence_note: The review also records cross-species potency differences it cannot explain (rats 50% of human insulin, dogs and pigs ~2x glargine). Animal half-lives (25-61 h vs 173 h human) from FDA 761326 PharmR 2026: "Following a single dose s.c. injection, terminal half-life ranged from 25 to 61 hours in rats, dogs, and LYD pigs and was 173 hours in humans."
dose.reason: Weekly target reached; animal t1/2 scaled short
dose.judgement: Same, not contra: the regimen the dog half-life screen was built to deliver (once-weekly) was reached in patients and worked (ONWARDS 1), so the dose target was met; the animals under-predicted the human half-life (173 h vs 61 h in the longest species, 25 h in rat), recorded as off_by_2-5x on the pig/dog bound (>5x on the rat). Icodec was selected by screening for long intravenous half-life in dogs (Kjeldsen 2021, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.1c00257). Efsitora's STZ rat (normoglycaemia for at least a week after one dose) likewise reached once-weekly dosing in humans (t1/2 ~17 days; FDA integrated review 2026). No member failed on exposure; insulin 338 reached glucose targets orally but at doses too large to manufacture, a cost not a PK failure (Halberg 2019). No toxicity margin was stated by the models, so margin_stated is null.
dose.magnitude_basis: terminal half-life: human 173 h vs 61 h (longest animal species)

dose.note: The STZ rat set peglispro's protraction target (longer duration of action than lispro, once-daily basal); human PK not yet paired.
dose.short: STZ rat sets peglispro protraction target
dose.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use (publication date of studies run before the 2011 phase 3 start).

dose.note: Peglispro's once-daily basal regimen was reached in humans (t1/2 24-45 h, flat profile, tolerated) and worked in IMAGINE 2; the rat's protraction target was met. Retrodiction ruling: peglispro's own human PK (Sinha 2014) was public before the rat paper (2016), so retro.
dose.quote: These results established a well-tolerated baseline dose for LY2605541 with a relatively flat PK profile and low intra-subject variability.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Human PK paper epub 2014-02-13; dated 2016 when the rat side was published. 'Worked' is IMAGINE 2 (Davies 2016, doi:10.1111/dom.12712, HbA1c non-inferior and superior to glargine). No rat half-life is given in the abstract, so no scaling magnitude.
dose.judgement: Same by the table's 'reached, drug worked' row: the regimen the rat's prolonged action was built to deliver (once-daily basal) was reached at a tolerated dose and the HbA1c primary was met. The rat stated no tolerability margin, so margin_stated is null. Peglispro was later stopped on liver safety, which is scored on the chronic toxicology track, not as a dose failure.
dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval supported by the duration of action (once daily)

dose.note: Efsitora's once-weekly regimen, read off the rat's >=1-week normoglycaemia, was reached and tolerated in humans; the rat t1/2 (~120 h) under-predicted the human ~17 days by ~3x. Dated 2022 (rule 6): NCT04450394 results posted 2022-11-02 showed the once-weekly regimen reached and tolerated, before Heise 2023.
dose.short: Weekly efsitora regimen reached; rat t1/2 ~3x short
dose.quote: BIF was well tolerated and the PK/PD profile enabled once-weekly dosing with minimal variation in exposure in a treatment interval of 1 week.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, sponsor-authored. Rat half-life ~120 h from the Moyers 2022 abstract (FDA 761408 integrated review gives 82-147 h); human ~17 days (~408 h), ratio ~3.4x. 'Worked' is the phase 2 (Bue-Valleskey 2023, NCT04450394) and QWINT-2 (NCT05362058).
dose.reason: Weekly target reached; rat t1/2 scaled short
dose.judgement: Strengthens the 2016 same with a second member: the rat said one dose holds normoglycaemia for at least a week, the once-weekly regimen was reached at tolerated doses and met its HbA1c primary in T2D, so the dose target was met; the rat under-predicted the human half-life about 3.4-fold, recorded as off_by_2-5x, the same direction as the Novo track's rat/dog/pig scaling for icodec. No tolerability margin was stated by the rat; hypoglycaemia in normoglycaemic toxicology animals is exaggerated pharmacology and is not a dose finding here.
dose.magnitude_basis: terminal half-life: STZ rat ~120 h vs human ~17 days (~408 h)

efficacy.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
efficacy.note: Pig clamp showed a flat, protracted glucose-lowering profile for degludec; no patient HbA1c result yet.
efficacy.quote: Action profile of insulin 454 (0.6 mM and 1.2 mM) or Glargine (0.6 mM). A euglycaemic clamp study in pigs [by Novo Nordisk A/S, Denmark]
efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy opening date (study dated March 2006; review public 2015).

efficacy.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
efficacy.note: BEGIN Once Long: degludec non-inferior to glargine on HbA1c at 52 weeks in 1,030 insulin-naive T2D patients; every later member also met its HbA1c primary. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same. Dated 2011 (rule 6, earliest date): the phase 2 trial (NCT00611884, HbA1c primary at 16 weeks, metformin background in all arms) already matched; BEGIN Once Long (2012) confirms and is in patient_trials.
efficacy.short: HbA1c non-inferior to glargine at 52 weeks
efficacy.quote: Insulin degludec provides comparable glycaemic control to insulin glargine without additional adverse events and might reduce dosing frequency due to its ultra-long action profile.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the pairing with the pig/rat/dog pharmacology is the drafter's, from the FDA pharmacology review.
efficacy.reason: Every member met its HbA1c primary
efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: no member whose animal data fell short then failed in patients. Peglispro met IMAGINE 2 (HbA1c difference -0.29%, NCT01435616) and was stopped for liver safety, not efficacy; oral insulin 338 matched glargine on fasting glucose in phase 2 (NCT02470039) and was stopped because the oral dose was too large to manufacture; icodec (ONWARDS 1) and efsitora (QWINT-2) were non-inferior. ex1000 could not be identified and is not scored. The pharmacology models predict glucose lowering, a surrogate; DEVOTE (NCT01959529, Marso 2017, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1615692) was a cardiovascular safety trial (MACE HR 0.91, non-inferior), not an outcome-benefit trial, so outcome_tested stays null. Direction only: treat-to-target trials do not test the magnitude the models predicted.

patient_trials.quote: Reduction in A1C with degludec was similar (noninferior) to that with glargine (1.06 vs. 1.19%)
Peglispro was non-inferior to glargine in HbA1c reduction [least-squares (LS) mean difference: -0.29%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.40, -0.19]

the estimated between-group difference (-0.19 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.36 to -0.03) confirmed the noninferiority (P<0.001) and superiority (P = 0.02) of icodec.
(estimated treatment difference, -0.09 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.22 to 0.04), findings that showed noninferiority.
Reduction in A1C with degludec was similar (noninferior) to that with glargine (1.06 vs. 1.19%), with an estimated treatment difference of degludec to glargine of 0.09% (95% CI -0.04 to 0.22).

efficacy.note: The STZ rat showed prolonged glucose lowering for peglispro; no patient HbA1c result paired yet.
efficacy.quote: BIL exhibited a markedly longer time to maximum concentration after subcutaneous injection, a greater area under the concentration-time curve, and a longer duration of action in the STZ-treated diabetic rat than insulin lispro.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use (publication date of studies run before the 2011 phase 3 start).

efficacy.note: IMAGINE 2: peglispro non-inferior (and superior) to glargine on HbA1c at 52 weeks in insulin-naive T2D, the glucose lowering the STZ rat predicted. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
efficacy.quote: Peglispro was non-inferior to glargine in HbA1c reduction [least-squares (LS) mean difference: -0.29%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.40, -0.19]
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; pairing with the rat is the drafter's. Registry results for NCT01435616 were posted 2018-04-13, after the paper (epub 2016-08-12).
efficacy.judgement: Same, not neg: the rat's own data for peglispro were not below the class bar (prolonged glucose lowering, full agonism) and the HbA1c primary was met. The programme was stopped on liver fat and ALT, a harm the single-dose rat study was not designed to show and that is scored once, on the rat/dog chronic toxicology track. Direction only: a treat-to-target trial does not test the magnitude a rat glucose curve predicts. The pharmacology predicts a surrogate; no outcome trial was run for peglispro.

patient_trials.quote: Peglispro was non-inferior to glargine in HbA1c reduction [least-squares (LS) mean difference: -0.29%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.40, -0.19]

efficacy.note: Efsitora phase 2 in insulin-naive T2D: HbA1c non-inferior to degludec at 26 weeks (results posted 2022-11-02); QWINT-2 confirmed at 52 weeks in 2024. Retrodiction ruling: insulin's (an INSR agonist's) glucose lowering in patients was public decades before this model's result, so the match is scored retro, not same.
efficacy.quote: After 26 weeks of treatment, BIF demonstrated a noninferior HbA1c change from baseline versus degludec, with a treatment difference of 0.06% (90% CI -0.11, 0.24; P = 0.56).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Dated 2022 by the registry results posting for NCT04450394 (2022-11-02), which preceded the paper (Diabetes Care, 2023); the rat side (Moyers 2022, epub 2022-07-15) was public by then. Pairing is the drafter's.
efficacy.reason: Both Lilly members met their HbA1c primary
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens with the second member: the rat predicted week-long glucose lowering for efsitora and the phase 2 and phase 3 (QWINT-2) HbA1c primaries in T2D were met against degludec. Direction only. The T1D trial (QWINT-5) also met its HbA1c primary but is another disease and is not scored here. No outcome trial has been run; outcome_tested stays null.

patient_trials.quote: After 26 weeks of treatment, BIF demonstrated a noninferior HbA1c change from baseline versus degludec, with a treatment difference of 0.06% (90% CI -0.11, 0.24; P = 0.56).
(estimated treatment difference, -0.09 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.22 to 0.04), findings that showed noninferiority.

safety.model: In vitro mitogenicity in L6-hIR, HMEC and Saos-2 cells
safety.note: Degludec was 5x less mitogenic than human insulin in L6-hIR cells and 3-6% as potent in human mammary cells; no patient neoplasm comparison yet.
safety.quote: Insulin 454 had a lower mitogenic potency than non-modified human insulin.
safety.confidence_note: The review does not date the mitogenicity studies; 2009 (BEGIN phase 3 start) is a proxy for when the package existed.

safety.note: Degludec's 52-week rat study at 5x human exposure, with NPH comparator, replaced a carcinogenicity bioassay; no patient harm comparison yet.
safety.short: 52-week rat study in lieu of bioassay
safety.quote: No treatment-related increases in incidences of hyperplasia, benign or malignant tumors were recorded in female mammary glands from rats dosed with insulin degludec
safety.confidence_note: Label text; the rat and dog studies were run before phase 3 (2009), so the model predates this entry.

safety.model: In vitro mitogenicity in L6-hIR, HMEC and Saos-2 cells
safety.note: FDA found no imbalance in neoplasm-related adverse events across the Tresiba/Ryzodeg phase 3 programme, as the low cell mitogenicity predicted.
safety.quote: In her review, she identified no imbalance across any of the above listed events that would preclude product approval.
safety.confidence_note: The quoted list includes neoplasm-related adverse events; the trials pool T1D and T2D. A predicted absence of harm is weak evidence of match, and the follow-up (1-2 years) is short for carcinogenesis.
safety.reason: Low mitogenicity; no neoplasm excess seen
safety.judgement: Same on a predicted absence: the cell assays said degludec was less mitogenic than human insulin and the phase 3 neoplasm counts showed no imbalance (DEVOTE, 7,637 patients over ~2 years, later reported no adverse-event difference). Icodec repeated the pattern (FDA 2026: reduced mitogenic potential, no carcinogenic potential in the 52-week rat, clinical malignancies reviewed). Efsitora (FDA 2026) showed a numerical excess of treatment-emergent malignancies (1.4% vs 1.0%) that the review team judged not causal (pre-existing disease, events within 90 days, reassuring nonclinical profile); recorded here, not scored, because the regulator found the model's prediction not contradicted. Pairing is the drafter's within one FDA package.
safety.magnitude_basis: neoplasm-related adverse events vs comparator insulin

safety.note: Peglispro's 52-week rat / 39-week dog studies reported no liver signal; T2D patients kept liver fat glargine cleared (2.6% difference) and ran higher ALT; Lilly stopped it. Retrodiction ruling: the toxicology data (Byrd 2017) were first public after peglispro's own patient liver data (2016) and failed to reproduce them, so contra stays, as a retrodiction.
safety.short: Liver fat, ALT rise missed in rat/dog tox
safety.quote: LS mean liver fat content was unchanged with peglispro at 52 weeks but decreased 3.1% with glargine [difference: 2.6% (0.9, 4.2); p = .002].
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides; the Byrd 2017 abstract lists standard pathology endpoints and reports no liver finding, but the full paper was not read. Dated 2017, when the toxicology data became public; the patient data were out in 2016 and Lilly's discontinuation press release in December 2015.
safety.reason: Rat/dog tox silent on hepatic fat, ALT
safety.judgement: Contra on a missed harm the species could show: hepatic steatosis and transaminase rise are routine rat/dog findings, and the chronic studies (4-6x clinical exposure, NPH comparator) were silent, yet across seven peglispro trials ALT was 7 IU/L higher than glargine and liver fat 2.2-5.3% higher at 52 weeks (Cusi 2016, doi:10.1111/dom.12751), the reason Lilly ended the programme. The harm is mechanistic (reduced peripheral insulin action raises free fatty acid flux to the liver, Mudaliar 2018, doi:10.1111/dom.13087) and so arguably predictable from the dog hepato-preferential clamp, which also did not flag it. The tox animals were normoglycaemic and not insulin-resistant, which may be why they were silent; that is a model limitation, not an excuse. Pairing is the drafter's. Degludec's 2013 MACE signal (FDA meta-analysis, HR up to 1.67) is not scored on this track: rat safety pharmacology cannot model atherothrombotic events in treat-to-target trials, and DEVOTE (2017) returned it to background (HR 0.91).

safety.note: Single-dose PK/PD in insulin-deficient rats; the study stated no harm prediction and reported none. Mitogenicity was read in cells (its own track).
safety.short: Single-dose STZ rat: no harm stated
safety.quote: Streptozotocin (STZ)-treated diabetic rats were used to study the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics of BIL.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; 2016 is a proxy for first use. Peglispro's liver harm is scored once, on the rat/dog chronic toxicology track, not here.

safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: T2D patients were measured, so their result sets the status. Severe hypoglycaemia was balanced (12 vs 14) and level 2/3 rate ratios 1.1-1.3 not significant; the single-dose STZ rat stated no harm, so untested. QWINT-5 (T1D, 10% vs 3% severe) is another disease.
safety.short: T2D hypoglycaemia balanced; rat stated no harm
safety.quote: Across the program, 12 efsitora-treated subjects experienced severe hypoglycemia compared with 14 comparator-treated subjects (Table 51 and Table 52).
safety.confidence_note: FDA 761408 IntegratedR 2026 (bundle lines 5820-5823); QWINT-2 registry results 2025-05-16 (NCT05362058). Former quote (QWINT-5, T1D): "Severe hypoglycaemia incidence was higher with efsitora (35 [10%] of 343) versus degludec (11 [3%] of 349) during weeks 0-52."
safety.judgement: Untested: the rat reported only normoglycaemia for at least a week after one dose and made no hypoglycaemia claim; the T2D programme did not show the harm, and the T1D excess cannot be imported where T2D patients were measured.

safety.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
safety.note: Novo's 2006 pig clamp profiled degludec's flat, protracted action against glargine; no hypoglycaemia comparison with patients yet.
safety.quote: Action profile of insulin 454 (0.6 mM and 1.2 mM) or Glargine (0.6 mM). A euglycaemic clamp study in pigs [by Novo Nordisk A/S, Denmark]
safety.confidence_note: Same bundle quote as the track's engagement opening (PharmR lines 2457-2459); study dated March 2006, review public 2015, so 2006 is a proxy.

safety.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
safety.note: The flat profile was expected to lower hypoglycaemia; BEGIN Once Long showed similar overall but lower nocturnal confirmed hypoglycaemia with degludec vs glargine. Retrodiction ruling: the model's hypoglycaemia prediction was first public in FDA's 2015 review, after degludec's own 2012 trial result, so retro (partial). Dating ruling: a paired comparison's year is the year its later side became public, here the FDA 2015 review, not the trial's 2012.
safety.quote: There were few episodes of nocturnal confirmed hypoglycemia in the overall population, and these occurred at a lower rate with degludec versus glargine (0.25 vs. 0.39 episodes/PYE; P = 0.038).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The prediction is stated in the FDA 2015 summary review (lines 707-709), drawn from the protracted flat profile shown in pig clamps and human PK/PD; overall confirmed hypoglycaemia was similar (1.52 vs 1.85/PYE), so partial.
safety.judgement: Same, partial: the stated prediction ('a protracted time-action profile that is relatively flat ... might enable true once-daily coverage with a lower risk of hypoglycemia', FDA 2015 SumR) held for nocturnal but not overall confirmed hypoglycaemia in BEGIN Once Long. Pairing is the drafter's, dated 2015, when its model side (FDA 2015 SumR) became public.
safety.magnitude_basis: nocturnal confirmed hypoglycaemia rate vs glargine

safety.model: LYD pig euglycaemic clamp + rat/dog PK
safety.note: Icodec, selected on the same protraction models, gave more level 2/3 hypoglycaemia than daily glargine in T2D (ONWARDS 1); FDA traces it to a day-2 peak after weekly dosing. Ruling: the pig clamp and PD models were never run under weekly dosing, so they made no prediction about a weekly day-2 hypoglycaemia peak; the comparison is untested, not contra. No icodec hypoglycaemia prediction is quotable, and degludec's 2015 claim does not carry across tracks. With no prediction there is nothing to retrodict, so not a retrodiction.
safety.quote: Rates of combined clinically significant or severe hypoglycemia were 0.30 events per person-year of exposure with icodec and 0.16 events per person-year of exposure with glargine U100
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Rate ratio 1.64 (0.98-2.75) at week 52, 1.63 (1.02-2.61) at week 83. FDA 761326 SumR 2026 (lines 184-186, 442-443) confirms higher level 2/3 rates on days 2-4; the 2024 T1D CRL for hypoglycaemia is the stronger signal but is another disease. Whether the class-level lower-hypoglycaemia claim was stated for icodec is inferred.
safety.judgement: Untested: icodec's pig/dog/rat data showed sustained, protracted glucose lowering (761326 PharmR lines 91-96) but no model was run under the weekly regimen the trial used, and none states a hypoglycaemia prediction for icodec. In patients the PD profile peaked on day 2 and level 2/3 hypoglycaemia was higher than with daily glargine (FDA 2026 SumR). Kept in the context's own T2D data, so no import.
